title: Developer Experience: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, Docs Site Operating Procedures, and Top Support Issues (Playbook)
author: Ava Martinez
body:
Overview
This playbook describes the standards and operational procedures for developer experience (DevEx) documentation maintained by the eng-developer-experience team. It covers: SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, representative API examples, docs-site operating procedures (CI/CD and publishing), and the top support issues we proactively document with canonical fixes. The goal is to ensure high-quality, discoverable documentation that reduces incoming support load and accelerates customer onboarding.

Goals
- Provide consistent, language-idiomatic SDK guides and reference examples for supported platforms (JS, Python, Go).
- Ship concise quickstarts and reusable templates for common integration patterns (chat, streaming, embeddings, reranking).
- Keep the docs site healthy and reliable with a reproducible CI/CD flow and clear rollback/runbook steps.
- Maintain a living list of top support issues, triage steps, and canonical fixes to reduce mean time to resolution for common problems.

Scope
- Public-facing SDK docs and quickstarts for the hosted API and SDKs maintained in GitHub repos: redwood-sdk-js, redwood-sdk-python, redwood-sdk-go.
- Internal docs-site operating procedures: build, preview, publish, monitor, and rollback.
- Top support issues: issues with clear reproducible symptoms and a deterministic canonical fix (or a documented mitigation).

Roles & Ownership
- Docs owner (primary): eng-developer-experience (content + release) — primary contact: Ava Martinez.
- SDK maintainer (code + API samples): owning SDK team (see repo README for owner aliases).
- Docs CI owner (infra for build/publish): eng-platform (dashboards-and-alerts).
- Support triage & canonical fixes: customer-success-and-support (integration with support playbook).

Standards for Content (mandatory checklist for each page)
1) Title and short description (one-line purpose).
2) Audience and required prerequisites (SDK versions, auth, minimal cloud/network requirements).
3) Step-by-step quickstart with copy-paste commands.
4) Minimal end-to-end example (requests + expected outputs).
5) Common failure modes + troubleshooting (symptom -> probable cause -> canonical fix).
6) Related links: SDK repo, issue templates, changelog, and relevant ADRs.
7) API contract snippets (JSON schemas, sample requests) when applicable.
8) Labels & metadata (language, product-surface, last-tested-version).

SDK Guides: structure and content recommendations
Each SDK guide page should be organized as:
- Intro & when to use this SDK
- Installation & compatibility table
- Authentication (examples for API key + env var + KMS/HSM note for Private deployments)
- Quickstart (5–10 minute copy-paste)
- Common patterns: streaming responses, function/tool calls, structured outputs, embedding+search
- Error handling and retries (status codes, backoff examples)
- Versioning and pinning guidance (how to pin major/minor releases)
- Migration notes for breaking changes

Sample installation & compatibility table (render in docs site as table):
- SDK: redwood-sdk-js | Latest tested: 1.6.x | Node: >=14 | Browser: supported (with bundler cautions)
- SDK: redwood-sdk-python | Latest tested: 0.9.x | Python: >=3.8
- SDK: redwood-sdk-go | Latest tested: 0.3.x | Go: >=1.19

Quickstarts & Templates
Deliverable templates (each as a repo/template and a docs page):
- Quickstart: Text generation (JS and Python) — minimal app that: authenticates, issues a generation request, displays streamed output.
- Quickstart: Chat + function/tool calling — demonstrates function schema + example of grounded tool call.
- Quickstart: Embeddings + semantic search — index small corpus, query, show top-k results.
- Template: Server-side API proxy (Express/FastAPI) — handles key rotation and token usage logging.
- Template: Edge/Browser-safe integration (token proxy + client snippet) — shows secure token exchange pattern.

File naming convention for quickstarts and templates:
- Use kebab-case, end with year: e.g., text-generation-quickstart-2026, embeddings-search-template-2026.

API Examples: canonical snippets and patterns
We keep a short set of canonical examples per language: generate, stream, function-call, embeddings, and rerank. Keep examples <= 30 lines of code where possible. Examples are hosted in SDK repos and embedded into docs using include directives.

Node.js (canonical generation example):
```js
import Redwood from 'redwood-sdk-js';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
const res = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-1b', prompt: 'Summarize the following text:' });
console.log(res.text);
```

Python (streaming example):
```py
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'])
for chunk in client.stream("chat.completions", model='redwood-chat-1.0', messages=[{'role':'user','content':'Write a haiku'}]):
    print(chunk.text, end='')
```

Docs Site Operating Procedures (CI/CD & runbook)
Primary stack: Docusaurus v2 (docs-site repo) + GitHub Actions (workflow: docs-ci) + Vercel preview for pull-requests + production deploy to a static host (Vercel/CloudFront).

Publishing checklist (pull request -> merge -> publish):
1) Create PR in docs-site with topical changes and previewable content. Enable Vercel preview.
2) Run local build to validate: `yarn build` and `yarn lint:md` (we require lint pass).
3) Ensure code snippets are validated against SDK fixtures where available (GH Action: snippets-validate).
4) Add reviewer(s) and label `docs:publish` for non-trivial changes.
5) After merge, docs-ci runs integration checks and deploys preview to production host. Monitor deployment job and CloudFront invalidation.

Rollback and emergency publish
- If a production deploy causes breakage (broken includes, incorrect frontmatter): revert the PR and trigger docs-ci manually: `gh workflow run docs-ci --repo org/docs-site --ref main`.
- For urgent fixes where CI is blocked, follow the emergency publish runbook: create a small single-file PR with `emergency-fix` label, require 1 reviewer from eng-developer-experience, and merge using the `docs-release` bot which bypasses scheduled checks. Document reasons in the PR description and notify #devex on Slack.

Docs health checks (daily/weekly):
- Broken link scanner (runs daily): threshold for alerts is >5 broken links in last 24h. Owner: eng-platform.
- Build failures: Pager duty to docs-ci-owner Slack on first failure.
- Snippet drift: weekly job checks that embedded snippets still compile against the latest SDK test fixtures. Failure creates a ticket in the SDK repo.

Top Support Issues and Canonical Fixes
We maintain a living list of the most frequent support issues with a concise triage and fix. Each entry should include: symptom, reproduction steps, root cause, canonical fix, and rollback/migration guidance. Keep examples reproducible with a minimal cURL.

Issue 1: Auth 401 on server-side calls\- Symptom: 401 responses immediately after integrating SDK in server runtime.\- Reproduction: Run `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'` and see 401.\- Root cause: Using a short-lived browser token (client-side) or misconfigured env var (`REDWOOD_APIKEY` vs `REDWOOD_API_KEY`).\- Canonical fix: Confirm using server API key in env var `REDWOOD_API_KEY`. For browser integrations, implement secure token-exchange proxy. Update quickstart template: server-proxy-template-2026.

Issue 2: Streaming response truncates early or SSE disconnects\- Symptom: Stream closes after a few tokens or connection resets intermittently.\- Reproduction: Use SDK streaming example with long output (>512 tokens).\- Root cause: Upstream load balancer idle timeout (NLB/ALB default 60s) or missing keepalive configuration in serverless functions.\- Canonical fix: Ensure LB idle timeout >= 300s for long streams. For serverless hosts, use chunked transfer encoding and keepalive headers. Document recommended infra settings in eng-infra/cloud-accounts-and-networking.

Issue 3: 429 Rate limit errors during batching experiments\- Symptom: Intermittent 429s when enabling aggressive client-side batching.\- Root cause: Client-side burst exceeds per-key rate limits; also check global per-customer quotas.\- Canonical fix: Implement exponential backoff with jitter (see snippet below) and configure SDK batching window to default 20ms. Request increased quota via dedicated-capacity channels for sustained throughput.
Backoff snippet (recommended):
```js
function backoff(retries) {
  return Math.min(1000 * Math.pow(2, retries) + Math.random() * 100, 10000);
}
```

Issue 4: Embeddings semantic drift (unexpected poor recall)\- Symptom: Search returns low-quality results after model upgrade.\- Root cause: Model variant change (different embedding geometry) without reindexing.\- Canonical fix: Recompute embeddings for the index when changing embedding model. Add a migration step to upgrade runbooks: reindex-job -> validate-top-k precision on a holdout set -> swap alias.

Issue 5: SDK version mismatch (Type errors in examples)\- Symptom: Examples in docs show APIs that no longer exist in latest SDK.\- Root cause: Docs not updated after SDK release.\- Canonical fix: Add SDK release gating to docs CI: every SDK release must bump `tested-sdk-versions` and run snippets-validate. If a mismatch is detected, mark docs page `needs-update` and assign to SDK owner.

Publishing and Review Process (detailed steps)
1) Author creates PR in docs-site or quickstart template repo.
2) Run `yarn build` and `snippets-validate` locally.
3) Select reviewers from the OWNERS file. Add labels: `docs:review`, `language:js` (if applicable).
4) After approvals, merge to main. CI will run checks and deploy; monitor job in GH Actions and Vercel logs.
5) If change touches SDK snippet, open cross-repo PR in the SDK repo linking the docs PR to ensure snippet compatibility.

Monitoring & Metrics
- Docs change lead time: median time from PR open -> merge <= 48 hours for non-major changes.
- Snippet drift rate: < 2% of snippets failing weekly.
- Support deflection rate: increase self-serve resolution measured by decrease in tickets referencing ‘how to’ docs.

Appendix: useful commands and examples
- Local build: `yarn && yarn build`
- Lint: `yarn lint:md`
- Run snippet validator (locally): `python tools/snippet_validator.py --fixtures ./sdk-fixtures`
- Trigger docs CI manually: `gh workflow run docs-ci --ref main`

Minimal cURL generation example (for troubleshooting):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -d '{"model":"redwood-1b","prompt":"Translate to French: Hello world"}'
```

Change log

Contacts & escalation

- Support triage: support-triage@redwood.example (customer-success-and-support).

Keywords: SDK guides, quickstart, template, API examples, docs CI, snippet validation, streaming, embeddings, rate limits, support deflection
